against: RUNBOOK section 3 craft rules, the seven faults, the recommended lesson shape, the course visual language (10 Oct) and CONCISION

findings.text: Says sixths 'measure neither' fraction. Wrong: 6 ÷ 2 = 3, so sixths measure the half exactly (3/6); they fail only on 3/4 (6 ÷ 4 is not whole). Fix: sixths measure the half but not the three-quarters.

'If your answer's bottom is bigger than both you started with, you have added the bottoms' is wrong: choosing the product piece (thirds and quarters → twelfths) legitimately gives a bottom bigger than both. Fix: the tell-tale is a bottom equal to the two bottoms added (2 + 4 = 6); the answer's bottom is the piece you chose and nothing else.
'With units the finer one always measures the coarser' fails for millimetres against inches (25.4). Restrict to metric units and say why (a metre is exactly 1000 mm).
'every time you add times on a job sheet you have been adding fractions in a matched piece': adding whole hours is not that. Narrow to adding minutes.

'the clock told you that long before any fraction did' is chat; and the worked numbers (2/4 + 3/4 = 5/4, 1 1/4) appear in p1 and again fully in p3. Keep p1 to the idea in one line, let p3 do the working once.

552 words, and it asks the builder to put '2 + 3 = 5 quarters, 5/4 = 1 1/4 h' as a label at one mark on a 340 px picture. Move the working to a line of working under the bars (a skill interactive is a worked example whose steps recompute), keep the mark's label short (5/4 h, or 75 min at the opening), and cut the sentence that repeats 'neither run changes length and the mark stays put'. Also say the bars have no cuts of their own at the opening setting, so the builder does not draw quarters there.
The take-away result is 'remainder' on the interactive and 'what is left' in explain and practice. Use 'what is left' everywhere; 'sum' for the add result.
'since 2 is 2/1 and 1 × 4 = 4 needs 2 × 4 = 8 on top' is hard to follow. Say: two whole metres are 2 × 4 = 8 quarters, so 2 is 8/4.

Checklist, rule of thumb, worked example (add and take away, real numbers computed from the rule), mistakes: all present. Takeaway all-bold with footnotes: present. Misconception (4/6) shown failing with numbers: present. Trade analogy with breaks: present. Causal why (tops count, bottoms name; counts add only of one piece; bottom is a name so it stays): present. Brief names the cause (count both in quarters) and the effect (the 1/2 run gains a cut, reads 2/4, tops 2 + 3 = 5 agree with the joined run). Citations each on words the quote supports. No new [[term]] needed: the lesson uses common denominator, equivalent fractions, improper fraction and mixed number from earlier lessons by name.

Two controls: piece (the cause) and Add/Take away. The idea is 'add or take away', and the take-away half cannot be seen without the switch, so it stays; the piece stepper stays first as the one he moves to see the effect.
